$comment: The PermissionRequest hook payload — the wire shape that turns a Claude Code permission prompt into an ANSWERABLE record. Two independent readers pick DIFFERENT fields off the same frame, so a CLI rename breaks only one of them unless both are pinned here. claudemon (session/state.rs::apply) reads tool_name/summary|message and is the ONLY thing that can put a PTY session into SessionMode::Approval; the desktop (main/services/sessionStore/hookEventRouter.ts) reads tool_name/tool_input/permission_suggestions to render the card the user actually clicks. Registration is normative too: claudemon init writes HookEventKind::REGISTERABLE into ~/.claude/settings.json, and while PermissionRequest was misfiled there as 'forward-compat only' the hook was never installed at all, so a PTY agent's permission prompt produced no approvable record and blocked forever. Verified against CLI 2.1.237.
